tests.name: DES supernova time dilation: pure energy-loss model
tests.note: Pure energy loss predicts b=0, while DES measures b=1.003±0.005(stat)±0.010(sys).

tests.name: DES time dilation: engineered pulse-stretch variant
tests.note: Adding an independent (1+z) pulse stretch passes this one observable but is no longer pure energy loss.

tests.name: CMB temperature at z=0.89: path-only static bath
tests.note: A path-only model predicts the local bath remains T0; ALMA measures 5.13±0.06 K.

tests.name: CMB temperature: globally evolving radiation field
tests.note: T(z)=T0(1+z) passes, but requires global cosmic evolution rather than distance-only loss.

tests.name: Distance duality: pure energy-loss static geometry
tests.note: At z=1 the model gives eta=2^-3/2; converted to the linear eta0 diagnostic it is far from PantheonPlus+BAO.

tests.name: Distance duality: energy loss plus pulse stretch
tests.note: Adding time dilation changes eta(z=1) to 1/2, still far from eta≈1 unless focusing/geometry also evolves.

tests.name: Stochastic collision broadening at z=1
tests.note: At R=140,000, a Poisson collision model needs >~10^10 tiny events to avoid resolvable broadening.

tests.name: Stationary redshift drift
tests.note: A stationary path-loss law predicts zero drift; current ESPRESSO uncertainty is still much too large.

tests.name: BAO Alcock-Paczynski geometry at z=2.33
tests.note: Static r∝ln(1+z) geometry differs by order 10%, larger than percent-level Ly-alpha BAO precision.

fatal_tests: DES supernova time dilation: pure energy-loss model
CMB temperature at z=0.89: path-only static bath
Distance duality: pure energy-loss static geometry
Distance duality: energy loss plus pulse stretch
verdict: The pure stationary continuous photon-energy-loss model is falsified. It can be repaired observable by observable only by adding pulse-time stretching, global radiation-temperature evolution, and evolving focusing/geometry. Those repairs turn it into an effective metric cosmology rather than a simple tired-light mechanism.
